description: The REPLACE statement's stacking phrases - format 1 REPLACE ALSO and format 2 REPLACE LAST OFF (§2023:7.2.4.2; the §2023:7.2.4.4 GR4-GR7 active / inactive-LIFO / canceled state machine). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the 1985 REPLACE is 'REPLACE { ==pseudo-text-1== BY ==pseudo-text-2== } …' or REPLACE OFF (§1985:XII.3.2), 'The format 2 REPLACE statement specifies that any text replacement currently in effect is discontinued' (§1985:XII.3.4 GR2) and 'A given occurrence of the REPLACE statement is in effect from the point at which it is specified until the next occurrence of the statement' (GR3) - no ALSO, no LAST, no stack; 2002 prints REPLACE [ ALSO ] and REPLACE [ LAST ] OFF (§2002:7.1.3.1): 'Once encountered, a format 1 REPLACE statement has one of three states' (§2002:7.1.3.3 GR4), 'A format 1 REPLACE statement with the ALSO phrase results in the following' (GR7a), 'A format 2 REPLACE statement with the LAST phrase cancels the active REPLACE statement and pops the last statement that was pushed into the queue of inactive REPLACE statements' (GR7c), and §2002:F.2 item 114 records 'REPLACE statement nesting. A REPLACE statement may be specified and terminated without canceling the effect of a previous REPLACE statement'. 2014 keeps them (§2014:7.2.3.3 GR4, GR7a, GR7c). ACTIVE since kb/Work PB1357: CopyProcessor.ApplyReplaceStatements parses both phrases and drives ReplaceStates; the introduction gate is its Gate() on the ALSO / LAST word (frontend, COBOL0900 below 2002).
vcr: 2002 introduction (§2002:7.1.3 format 1 ALSO / format 2 LAST; §2002:F.2 item 114)
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VMRAL.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 AA PIC X(2) VALUE "AA".
01 BB PIC X(2) VALUE "BB".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
REPLACE ==XX1== BY ==AA==.
REPLACE ALSO ==XX2== BY ==BB==.
    DISPLAY XX1 XX2.
REPLACE LAST OFF.
    DISPLAY XX1.
REPLACE OFF.
    STOP RUN.
